description: MoonMatrix is a team dedicated to inspiring future space explorers through innovative learning experiences. Our project, Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer, will provide interactive astronaut training, mission simulations, and space education tools. We welcome collaborators interested in web development, UI/UX design, graphic design, content creation, and space technology. Together, we aim to make astronaut training engaging, accessible, and fun for everyone.
summary:
unior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based simulation game designed for children ages 7–12 to experience the engineering challenges of living on the Moon and Mars. Players select an astronaut specialist and establish an outpost at real NASA landing sites—Shackleton Crater on the Moon or Jezero Crater on Mars—where they must balance battery power, oxygen generation, and radiation shielding across 10 Sols.

The application addresses the challenge by translating real NASA datasets—including live space weather alerts from the NASA DONKI API, lunar telemetry from LRO/Moon Trek, and Martian surface data from Perseverance (MEDA/MOXIE)—into intuitive gameplay mechanics. When solar flares, coronal mass ejections, or dust storms strike, young learners make critical power-allocation trade-offs and unlock bite-sized "Did You Know?" science facts explaining the real physics behind each decision.

By turning complex space mission engineering into a visual, trial-and-error experience with zero installation barriers, this tool inspires the next generation of explorers to think like NASA engineers and understand what it takes to sustain human life beyond Earth.
details:
Project Details: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

1. What does it do and how does it work?

Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based simulation game designed for children ages 7–12 to experience real-world space mission engineering on the Moon and Mars.

  • The Core Gameplay Loop: Players choose an astronaut specialist and establish an outpost at authentic NASA landing sites—Shackleton Crater (Moon) or Jezero Crater (Mars). Across 10 Sols, players must balance three vital survival resources: Battery Power (kWh), Oxygen & Greenhouse (%), and Radiation Shielding (%) using real-time power-allocation sliders.
  • Dynamic Hazard & Event System: The game dynamically triggers space weather events (such as M-class solar flares, coronal mass ejections, and dust storms) driven by real NASA data, forcing players to make critical engineering trade-offs (e.g., diverting energy from life support to activate magnetic shielding).
  • Traceable Science Integration: Every decision triggers an educational "Did You Know? Real NASA Science" popup explaining the underlying physics and aerospace engineering concepts.

2. What benefits and intended impact does it have?

  • Inspiring Young Learners: Translates complex space science and systems engineering into an engaging, accessible format that sparks curiosity in STEM for children ages 7–12.
  • Zero Barrier to Entry: Because it requires no downloads, installations, or logins, it can be deployed instantly in classrooms or at home by teachers, students, and judges alike.
  • Experiential Problem-Solving: Teaches kids why space agencies must carefully balance resources and protect astronauts from cosmic hazards, fostering critical thinking and resourcefulness.

3. What tools, coding languages, software, or hardware were used?

  • Frontend & UI: HTML5, CSS3, and Tailwind CSS (via CDN) for a responsive, colorful, child-friendly dashboard and animated SVG habitat graphics.
  • Game Logic & Simulation: JavaScript (ES6+) powering the Sol-by-Sol resource tick-down engine, hazard event triggers, and Web Audio API synthesis for immersive sound effects.
  • Data Sources & APIs: Integrated live NASA DONKI API endpoints (for real solar flare and CME data) with an automatic fallback curated dataset, alongside lunar telemetry from NASA LRO / Moon Trek and Martian surface parameters from Mars 2020 Perseverance (MEDA & MOXIE).
  • Hosting & Deployment: Hosted via GitHub Pages and packaged in a clean, maintainable single-file architecture.

4. How is your project creative and what factors did your team consider?

  • Translating Raw Data into Play: Instead of overwhelming children with raw scientific tables or complex code, we creatively mapped real NASA telemetry and space weather metrics into intuitive game parameters and visual hazard events.
  • Accessibility & UX Considerations: Designed with bright color-coded gauges, smooth animations, and clear visual feedback so young users of varying reading levels can easily grasp cause-and-effect relationships without frustration.
  • Offline Reliability: To prevent hackathon API rate limits or connection drops during judging, we engineered a seamless dual-mode system that queries live NASA DONKI data with an instant fallback to embedded JSON datasets, ensuring a 100% crash-free demo experience.
